_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.279: Simulator queues with complete trial recordings.

The Simulator tab verifies the ProSim 8 mini-USB DEVICE connection, previews large
BP/heart-rate/volume/envelope-shift queues, and runs the selected product preset
once per trial. Defaults are 120/80 mmHg, 72 bpm, 1 mL. MAP is calculated. Adult
and Neonatal waves require confirmation on the ProSim screen. Cuff, mandrel and
notes accompany dated setting-specific Arduino, native NI and ProSim files.
Each trial is followed by a verified vented 30-second break. Existing Bench tools
remain available. STOP and recording/link failures retain partial data and stop
the queue. Native NI time remains the reference; calibration history is retained.

Arm/Wrist CVP use gentler continuous rate correction to reduce valve open/close
hunting during slow deflation, through the shared GUI/standalone path. Control
limits, deadlines and safety signals remain unchanged. Two real Arm CVP trials
showed continuous valve opening through the low-pressure range. Acoustic silence,
all simulator rates and production fleet reliability are not established by this
limited bench check.

Validation: 1,421 source tests passed (6 skipped); all 13 offline gates passed.
The protected Device D snapshot/flash/restore retained calibration and control
values. The seed-213 soak exercised all five presets across six cycles for over
ten minutes: all scored cycles and PID segments passed, with 29,505/29,505
telemetry messages delivered (100.00%).

The final two pulse-enabled Arm CVP trials (70/15 and 70/20, Adult, 1 mL) both
completed, with a 30.266-second verified vented interval. After correcting the
simulator command order, NI pulse fits measured 72.02 and 72.01 bpm for the
requested 72 bpm. No valve reversals occurred from 40 to 5 mmHg and no abrupt
envelope step was detected in reliable windows. Pulses became unresolved below
about 15 mmHg; this does not establish preservation at every pressure or rate.
NI sampling remained contiguous at 500 Hz. Periodic signals do not establish
absolute sensor delay; the diagnostic reports ambiguous timing rather than
moving the NI reference clock.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
